title: Simulation of Half-Wave Rectifier in MATLAB/Simulink

questions.a: Rectification is the conversion of bidirectional alternating current (AC) into unidirectional pulsating direct current (DC).

questions.q: Why is the efficiency of a half-wave rectifier limited to 40.6%?
questions.a: Because the entire negative half-cycle of the AC input wave is blocked and wasted, and power is only delivered during the positive half-cycle.

questions.q: How does a capacitor connected across the load reduce ripple in a half-wave rectifier?
questions.a: The capacitor charges to V_peak during the positive peak and discharges slowly through the load resistor R1 with time constant R1*C1 when the diode is off, keeping V_out near V_peak.

questions.q: What is the Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) rating required for the diode in a half-wave rectifier?
questions.a: Without filter, PIV = V_m. With a capacitor filter, PIV = 2 * V_m because the cathode stays charged near +V_m while the anode swings to -V_m.

questions.q: What is the output ripple frequency of a half-wave rectifier driven by a 50 Hz AC supply?
questions.a: 50 Hz (equal to the input AC frequency f), because there is one output pulse per full AC cycle.

questions.q: How do you declare a 10 V, 50 Hz sinusoidal source in PySpice?
How is the filter capacitor C1 connected relative to the load resistor R1?
questions.a: In parallel (across) the load resistor R1, between Node 2 and GND.

questions.q: For a 15 V peak AC input and a silicon diode (0.7 V drop), what are V_peak_out and V_dc (unfiltered)?
What happens to the output waveform if diode D1 is reversed in a half-wave rectifier?
questions.a: The positive half-cycles are blocked and the negative half-cycles pass through, producing a negative half-wave rectified output.

questions.q: What happens to the ripple voltage if the filter capacitance C1 is increased?
questions.a: The time constant R1*C1 increases, so the capacitor discharges less between peaks and the peak-to-peak ripple voltage decreases.
